title: Ulyana and the Asset
premise: Sable Halloran, a ghost-employed financial-crimes investigator whose cases are quietly laundered into other agencies' wins, receives a call on a burner phone from Ulyana Petrova—a whistleblower they once protected and believed dead. Ulyana is alive, hiding in Riga, and holding a ledger that proves a trilateral sanctions-evasion network run through the very institutions Sable reports to. As an assassin named Voss closes in and three governments race to bury the evidence, Sable must choose between the invisibility that has kept them safe and the exposure that could finally deliver justice. The story ends with Sable broadcasting the ledger publicly, sacrificing their career and anonymity, while Ulyana—her identity permanently erased—walks free into a new life, and Voss, betrayed by his employers, becomes the next name on someone else's list.
about_author: Oscar Almeida is a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money across borders before turning to fiction full-time. He writes thrillers about people the system forgets it employs.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. In London, Sable closes another case only to watch credit for it vanish into a rival agency's press release. Establishes their invisible role, meticulous methods, and quiet resentment. Emotional beat: competent loneliness—the sense of being used without being seen.

chapters.title: The Number That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A burner phone appears in Sable's desk drawer, unregistered and impossible to trace. When it rings, a voice they buried years ago says their real name. Emotional beat: dread curdling into hope—the past isn't dead after all.

chapters.title: Ulyana
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, Riga. Ulyana reveals she faked her death after the witness-protection program sold her out, and she's been building a ledger of the sanctions-evasion network ever since. She needs Sable because they're the only analyst who can read it. Emotional beat: wary reunion between two people who trusted each other once and paid for it.

chapters.title: Ledger of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable decrypts fragments of the ledger overnight and recognizes shell structures they personally flagged years ago—cases that were killed from above. Someone inside their own chain of command is complicit. Emotional beat: vertigo as the ground of Sable's professional world gives way.

chapters.title: Three Flags
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Flashback chapter: how Ulyana survived the assassination attempt in Tallinn and who saved her—a disgraced intelligence officer now dead. Explains her resources and her isolation. Emotional beat: grief hardened into purpose.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Introduce the assassin: methodical, professional, contracted by a consortium with clients in three governments. He's given Sable's file and told to make it look like suicide. Emotional beat: cold competence masking a first flicker of doubt about his employers.

chapters.title: The Quiet Audit
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable covers their tracks at work while secretly copying files, using their knowledge of audit trails to buy time. A colleague notices something off. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into focus—Sable realizes invisibility is now a weapon.

chapters.title: Riga, Rain
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable flies to Riga under a work pretext and meets Ulyana in person for the first time in six years. They argue about trust; Ulyana tests whether Sable was followed. Emotional beat: fragile reconnection, two ghosts recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Buys
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana explains her endgame: not money, but public release—justice outside any court that would bury the case. Sable pushes back, wanting legal channels. Emotional beat: ideological friction between lawful instinct and earned cynicism.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss arrives in Riga and picks up Sable's trail through a hotel payment anomaly. He observes rather than strikes, reporting back—and notices his handlers asking questions that suggest Sable isn't the real target. Emotional beat: professional unease deepening.

chapters.title: The Colleague
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Back in London, Sable's colleague Priya confronts them with what she's found—and offers help instead of reporting them. Priya becomes Sable's inside line. Emotional beat: unexpected alliance; belonging offered where betrayal was expected.

chapters.title: Dead Drop Protocol
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana and Sable set up a dead-drop system to move ledger copies across borders, exploiting banking-reporting loopholes Sable knows intimately. First copy goes out. Emotional beat: cautious triumph—the machine of clean money turned against its owners.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss intercepts the courier but finds the package contains a decoy—and a message addressed to him by name, proving Ulyana knows exactly who he is. His employers realize he's compromised. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing he's also prey.

chapters.title: Priya's Price
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Priya is suspended after an internal leak hunt; Sable realizes their cover is blown inside the agency. They must move the final ledger piece before security locks everything down. Emotional beat: guilt and urgency—innocents are paying for Sable's choices.

chapters.title: The Safe House Burns
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Consortium operatives hit Ulyana's Riga safe house. She escapes with the master key but loses her archive backup; Voss, ordered to assist, deliberately lets her slip away. Emotional beat: terror and fury, and the strange mercy of an enemy's hesitation.

chapters.title: Convergence
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable and Ulyana regroup in Vilnius with only one complete copy of the ledger left. They learn the consortium plans to trigger a financial incident to destroy the evidence's credibility. Emotional beat: cornered resolve—no more exits, only forward.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Bought
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss confronts his handler and discovers he was always meant to die alongside the targets—a cleanup asset. He defects, bringing authentication codes that can verify the ledger. Emotional beat: bitter self-recognition; the tool choosing to become a person.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Night
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Sable attempts simultaneous disclosure to journalists and regulators in three countries while Ulyana runs interference and Voss feeds them the codes. Communications get cut; the plan starts failing in real time. Emotional beat: desperate momentum against a closing wall.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Cornered in a Vilnius data center, Sable uploads the verified ledger to mirror sites worldwide as Voss holds off the consortium's cleaners. The truth goes out and cannot be recalled. Emotional beat: catharsis through sacrifice—visibility chosen at last, whatever it costs.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Arrests ripple across three capitals; the consortium burns its own to survive. Ulyana watches from a crowd, officially still dead, and chooses to stay that way—not erasure but freedom. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; justice delivered without a name attached.

chapters.title: Resignation Letter
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable turns themselves in, confesses everything, and faces inquiry—but public opinion and Priya's testimony reshape the narrative. Stripped of career, Sable feels lighter than they have in years. Emotional beat: identity rebuilt on choice rather than concealment.

chapters.title: A Table for Two
chapters.summary: Dual POV, epilogue. Months later, in a small café far from anywhere, Sable meets a woman with a new name and no past. No ledgers, no phones, no debts. Emotional beat: belonging found between two people who finally exist on their own terms.
